# How to Calculate In-Hand Salary from CTC in India — Step-by-Step Formula with Examples


October 8, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/how-to-calculate-in-hand-salary-from-ctc-in-india-step-by-step-formula-with-examples/#respond)


You just got an offer letter that says ₹8 LPA CTC. Exciting, right? But when the first salary hits your bank account, it’s nowhere close to ₹66,667 per month. What happened to the rest?


The gap between your CTC (Cost to Company) and your actual in-hand salary catches almost every employee off guard ,freshers and experienced professionals alike. On average, your take-home pay is only 65–75% of your CTC, depending on your salary level and tax regime.


In this guide, we’ll break down the exact formula to calculate your in-hand salary from CTC, walk you through real examples at different salary levels, and show you how every rupee of your CTC is split — so you never feel confused looking at your salary slip again.


**Want a quick answer?** Use our free[In-Hand Salary Calculator](https://salarybox.in/salary-calculator/) to get your take-home pay in seconds.


#### **What Is CTC (Cost to Company)?**


CTC is the **total amount your employer spends on you in a year** . It includes everything — your monthly salary, employer’s PF contribution, gratuity, insurance premiums, bonuses, and any other benefits.


**CTC = Gross Salary + Employer’s PF Contribution + Employer’s ESI + Gratuity + Insurance + Other Benefits**


The key thing to understand: **CTC is NOT what you receive.** A significant portion goes towards statutory contributions (PF, ESI, gratuity) and taxes that never reach your bank account.


**Related Read:**[Decoding Cost to Company (CTC) — Understanding the True Value of Your Salary Package](https://salarybox.in/blog/decoding-cost-to-company-ctc-understanding-the-true-value-of-your-salary-package/)


**What Is In-Hand Salary (Take-Home Pay)?**


In-hand salary — also called take-home salary or net salary — is the **actual amount credited to your bank account** every month after all deductions.


**In-Hand Salary = Gross Salary − Employee PF − Employee ESI − Professional Tax − Income Tax (TDS)**


This is the money you can actually spend, save, or invest.


#### **CTC vs. In-Hand Salary — Key Differences**


**Parameter** **CTC** **In-Hand Salary**


Full Form Cost to Company Take-Home Pay / Net Salary


Includes Everything the employer spends Only what you receive in bank


PF included? Yes (employer + employee both) No (employee PF is deducted)


Tax included? No Yes (TDS is deducted)


Gratuity included? Yes No (paid only after 5 years)


Insurance included? Yes (if employer provides) No


Typical % 100% 65–78% of CTC


#### **Components of CTC — Where Does Your Money Go?**


Before jumping into the formula, you need to understand every component of your CTC. Here’s a complete breakup:


##### **A. Components You Receive (Direct Pay)**


**1. Basic Salary**


- Typically 40–50% of CTC
- Fully taxable
- This is the base for calculating PF, HRA, and gratuity


**2. House Rent Allowance (HRA)**


- Usually 40–50% of basic salary
- Partially or fully tax-exempt if you pay rent (under Section 10(13A) of old regime)


**3. Dearness Allowance (DA)**


- Common in government and older companies
- Fully taxable


**4. Special Allowance**


- Whatever is left after basic + HRA + other fixed allowances
- Fully taxable


**5. Other Allowances**


- Conveyance Allowance, Medical Allowance, Leave Travel Allowance (LTA), Meal Allowance
- Some have partial tax exemptions under the old regime


**Related Read:**[What Are Allowances in Salary — Types and Examples](https://salarybox.in/blog/what-are-allowances-in-salary-types-and-examples/)


##### **B. Components You Don’t Receive Directly**


**6. Employer’s Provident Fund (EPF) Contribution**


- 12% of basic salary (capped at ₹15,000 basic per month = ₹1,800/month max)
- Goes to your PF account, not your bank account


**7. Employee’s Provident Fund (EPF) Contribution**


- 12% of basic salary (same cap)
- Deducted from your gross salary


**8. Employer’s ESI Contribution**


- 3.25% of gross salary
- Applicable only if your gross salary is ≤ ₹21,000/month


**9. Employee’s ESI Contribution**


- 0.75% of gross salary
- Deducted from your gross salary
- Applicable only if your gross salary is ≤ ₹21,000/month


**10. Gratuity**


- 4.81% of basic salary (formula: Basic × 15/26 × 1 year)
- You receive this only after completing 5 years of service


**11. Insurance Premium**


- Group health or term insurance paid by employer
- Part of CTC but not your take-home


**Related Read:**[EPF Contributions — How They’re Calculated (Guide for Employees)](https://salarybox.in/blog/epf-contributions-calculated-guide-employees/)


##### **C. Deductions from Your Salary**


**12. Professional Tax**


- State-level tax, varies by state
- Maximum ₹2,500 per year (₹200/month in most states)


**13. Income Tax (TDS)**


- Deducted monthly by your employer based on your declared investments
- Calculated as per income tax slabs (see section below)


**Related Read:**[TDS on Salaries — A Comprehensive Guide for Employers](https://salarybox.in/blog/tds-on-salaries-a-comprehensive-guide-for-employers/)


#### **Step-by-Step Formula: How to Calculate In-Hand Salary from CTC**


Here is the exact 5-step process:


**Step 1: Identify Your CTC**


Start with your annual CTC from your offer letter or salary structure. Example: ₹8,00,000 per year.


**Step 2: Separate Employer-Side Costs from Gross Salary**


**Gross Salary = CTC − Employer’s PF − Employer’s ESI − Gratuity − Insurance Premium**


These are amounts your employer pays on your behalf but you never see in your bank account.


**Step 3: Calculate Your Basic Salary**


Most companies set basic salary at **40% to 50% of CTC** . In our formula, we’ll use 50% (which is the most common under the new wage code).


**Basic Salary = 50% of Gross Salary**


**Step 4: Calculate All Deductions**


Add up these deductions from your gross salary:


**Deduction** **How to Calculate**


Employee PF 12% of Basic (max ₹1,800/month if basic capped at ₹15,000)


Employee ESI 0.75% of Gross (only if gross ≤ ₹21,000/month)


Professional Tax ₹200/month (varies by state, see table below)


Income Tax (TDS) Based on tax slabs after exemptions


**Step 5: Subtract Deductions from Gross Salary**


**Monthly In-Hand Salary = Monthly Gross Salary − Employee PF − Employee ESI − Professional Tax − Monthly TDS**


That’s your take-home pay.

Let’s work through four real examples at different salary levels. All examples use the **new tax regime for FY 2026-27** and assume:


- Basic Salary = 50% of Gross
- HRA = 40% of Basic
- Employer PF = 12% of Basic (capped at ₹15,000 basic)
- Standard Deduction = ₹75,000

**Income Tax Slabs for FY 2026-27 — New Regime vs. Old Regime**


Tax is the biggest deduction for employees earning above ₹12 LPA. Here’s a comparison of both regimes:


**New Tax Regime (Default) — FY 2026-27**


**Taxable Income Slab** **Tax Rate**


Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil


₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 5%


₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 10%


₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 15%


₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 20%


₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 25%


Above ₹24,00,000 30%


- **Standard Deduction:** ₹75,000
- **Rebate (Sec 156):** No tax if taxable income ≤ ₹12,00,000
- **Cess:** 4% on total tax


**Old Tax Regime (Opt-In)**


**Taxable Income Slab** **Tax Rate (Below 60 Years)**


Up to ₹2,50,000 Nil


₹2,50,001 to ₹5,00,000 5%


₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 20%


Above ₹10,00,000 30%


- **Standard Deduction:** ₹50,000
- **Rebate (Sec 156):** No tax if taxable income ≤ ₹5,00,000
- **Allows deductions:** 80C (₹1.5L), 80D, HRA exemption, LTA, etc.


**Which Regime Should You Choose?**


**Choose the New Regime if:**


- Your salary is below ₹12 LPA (effectively zero tax)
- You don’t have a home loan, high rent, or significant investments


**Choose the Old Regime if:**


- You claim HRA exemption for high rent payments
- You have a home loan (Section 24 interest deduction)
- You invest heavily in 80C instruments (PPF, ELSS, etc.)
- Your total deductions exceed ₹3.75 lakh per year

**7 Smart Tips to Maximise Your In-Hand Salary**


**1. Negotiate a Higher Basic Salary**


A higher basic means higher PF contribution and better gratuity, but if you want more in-hand, ask for a **lower basic and higher special allowance** (since PF is calculated on basic).


**2. Claim Full HRA Exemption (Old Regime)**


If you pay rent, submit rent receipts to your employer. HRA exemption can save ₹50,000–₹2,00,000 in tax per year depending on your rent and city.


**Related Read:**[HRA Calculator — Check Your HRA Exemption](https://salarybox.in/hra-calculator/)


**3. Opt for Meal Coupons / Food Allowance**


Meal allowances up to ₹50 per meal are tax-free. Over a year, that’s about ₹26,400 saved.


**4. Use the NPS Benefit**


Under the new regime, employer’s NPS contribution up to 14% of salary is tax-free. Ask if your employer offers this.


**5. Declare Investments Early**


Submit your investment declarations (Form 12BB) at the start of the financial year. This ensures your employer deducts less TDS each month, increasing your monthly in-hand.


**6. Review Your Salary Structure**


If your company gives you flexibility, restructure your CTC to maximise tax-free components. Every company has a different policy, so ask HR.


**7. Use Tax-Saving Instruments (Old Regime)**


If you choose the old regime, invest in:


- PPF, ELSS, or NPS for Section 80C (up to ₹1.5L)
- Health insurance for Section 80D (up to ₹25,000–₹1L)
- Home loan interest under Section 24 (up to ₹2L)


**Related Read:**[Tax Benefits of Investing in PPF — Exemptions & Deductions](https://salarybox.in/blog/tax-benefits-investing-ppf-exemptions-deductions/)


**How Employers Structure CTC — What HR Won’t Tell You**


Understanding how your employer designs your CTC helps you negotiate better:


**High Basic (50% of CTC):**


- More PF, more gratuity, more HRA exemption
- But also more taxable income and more deductions


**Low Basic (30–40% of CTC):**


- Lower PF deduction = more in-hand pay
- But lower retirement savings and lower HRA exemption


**Performance Bonus / Variable Pay in CTC:**


- Many companies include 10–20% of CTC as variable/bonus
- This is NOT guaranteed — it depends on performance
- Your real “fixed” in-hand is even lower


**Tip:** Always ask for the **fixed vs. variable split** before accepting an offer. A ₹12 LPA CTC with ₹2L variable pay means your guaranteed salary is only ₹10 LPA.

**Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)**


**What percentage of CTC is in-hand salary?**


Typically, your in-hand salary is **65% to 85% of your CTC** , depending on your salary level, tax regime, and employer’s CTC structure. At lower CTCs (below ₹12L), in-hand is higher (80–92%) because of the tax rebate. At higher CTCs (₹25L+), it drops to 74–84% due to higher tax.


**What is the formula to convert CTC to in-hand salary?**


Where: **Gross Salary = CTC − Employer PF − Employer ESI − Gratuity − Insurance**


**Is CTC and in-hand salary the same?**


No. CTC is the total cost your employer bears, including PF, gratuity, insurance, and benefits. In-hand salary is what actually gets deposited in your bank account after all deductions. CTC is always higher than in-hand salary.


**How to calculate monthly take-home salary?**


Divide your annual in-hand salary by 12. Or use this shortcut: **Monthly Take-Home = (Monthly Gross) − (Monthly PF + Professional Tax + Monthly TDS)** . For a quick calculation, use our[In-Hand Salary Calculator](https://salarybox.in/salary-calculator/) .


**Is PF deducted from CTC or salary?**


PF is part of your CTC. The employer’s PF contribution (12% of basic) is included in CTC but not in your gross salary. The employee’s PF contribution (another 12% of basic) is deducted from your gross salary. So PF impacts your in-hand from both sides.


**What deductions reduce in-hand salary the most?**


For employees earning above ₹15 LPA, **income tax (TDS) is the largest deduction** , often 15–25% of gross salary. For lower earners, **employee PF** is the biggest deduction. Professional tax (₹200/month) has minimal impact.


**Can I opt out of PF to increase in-hand salary?**


If your basic salary exceeds ₹15,000/month, you can request your employer to opt out of EPF. However, this means losing retirement savings and employer’s matching contribution. Most financial advisors recommend staying in PF.


**How does the new tax regime affect in-hand salary?**


Under the new regime, employees with taxable income up to ₹12,00,000 pay zero tax (due to the rebate under Section 156). The standard deduction is ₹75,000 — which means employees with gross salary up to about ₹12,75,000 effectively pay no income tax. This significantly boosts in-hand salary for earners below ₹12 LPA CTC.

**Conclusion**


Calculating your in-hand salary from CTC doesn’t have to be complicated. Here’s the simple version:


1. **Start with your CTC**
2. **Subtract employer-side costs** (employer PF, gratuity, ESI, insurance) → this gives your **Gross Salary**
3. **Subtract employee deductions** (employee PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS) → this gives your **In-Hand Salary**


As a rule of thumb:


- **Below ₹12L CTC** → Expect 82–92% in-hand (almost no tax)
- **₹12L–₹20L CTC** → Expect 85–89% in-hand
- **₹20L–₹50L CTC** → Expect 74–84% in-hand
